principle: Candidate-facing options, stored schemas, vacancy options and comparators must use the same canonical scale.

questions.Question: I understand that SHEXON will create a Talent Fit Profile from information I provide, my CV and structured conversations.
I understand that SHEXON may compare my profile with vacancy requirements and use vacancy-specific company weights to produce an internal ranking.
I understand that AI may assist with extraction, organisation and draft summaries, while SHEXON staff review the result before any introduction.
I understand that vacancy information that is not specified will be treated as unknown, not assumed.
I understand that SHEXON will ask me before sharing my Candidate Fit Brief with a named employer.
I confirm that I can review and correct my profile and request information about how a match was generated.
What is your current country of residence?
For your next role, do you expect to need employer visa sponsorship?
questions.Options / scale: Yes / No / I am not sure

questions.Question: What is the earliest date you could start?
Which opportunity types are you considering?
Which working languages can you use professionally?
Which work arrangements are acceptable to you?
Which three job titles or role families are closest to what you want next?
Are you actively looking, open to relevant opportunities, or exploring for later?
questions.Options / scale: Active / Open / Exploring / Not currently available

questions.Question: Upload your current CV or experience profile.
Is there anything practical that should be checked before we contact you about a role?
What is the primary role direction you want to move toward in the next 12–24 months?
What is your second acceptable role direction?
Which kinds of problems do you most enjoy solving?
questions.Options / scale: Analytical / technical / operational / customer / commercial / people / creative / process / research / other

questions.Question: Which work activities would you like to do more often in your next role?
Which activities would you prefer not to become the majority of your role?
Which industries are you actively interested in?
Which skills or experiences do you most want to develop next?
What would make you consider a role that is outside your first-choice direction?
Describe one role you would not accept even if the title or salary looked attractive. Why?
Rank the five factors that would most influence whether you stay engaged in a role.
questions.Options / scale: Learning / ownership / stability / progression / impact / technical depth / variety / autonomy / recognition / financial reward / leadership / collaboration

questions.Question: For each selected factor, choose the range you would ideally like a role to provide.
questions.Response: Preferred minimum and maximum for each selected factor

questions.Question: For each selected factor, choose the wider range you could still accept.
questions.Response: Tolerable minimum and maximum for each selected factor
questions.Options / scale: 1 very limited – 5 very strong; must contain the preferred range

questions.Question: For each selected factor, what would a good level look like in practice?
questions.Response: Short open text repeated five times

questions.Question: For each selected factor, give one experience showing why it matters to you.
Which selected factor, if below your tolerable minimum, would most likely make you leave within a year?
questions.How used: Priority boundary; does not become an automatic gate

questions.Question: Tell us about a project or experience where you stayed highly engaged after the initial excitement passed. What sustained it?
Tell us about work or study that drained your energy. Which conditions mattered most?
How clearly do you prefer goals and responsibilities to be defined when you start a task?
How often can priorities change before the work becomes frustrating rather than energising?
questions.Options / scale: Rarely / monthly / weekly / several times weekly / daily

questions.Question: How much freedom do you prefer in deciding how to complete your work?
How frequently do you prefer your manager to check in while you are learning a new role?
questions.Options / scale: Daily / several times weekly / weekly / every two weeks / monthly

questions.Question: After you are established in a role, how frequently do you prefer feedback?
questions.Options / scale: Weekly / every two weeks / monthly / quarterly / when needed

questions.Question: Which process environment suits you best?
questions.Options / scale: Established / mostly established / mixed / mostly being built / no established processes

questions.Question: Which role breadth do you prefer?
questions.Options / scale: Deep specialist / specialist with variety / balanced / broad generalist

questions.Question: How much direct stakeholder interaction do you prefer?
questions.Options / scale: Limited / occasional / regular / substantial / most of the role

questions.Question: Which working pace suits you best?
questions.Options / scale: Predictable / mostly planned / mixed / fast-changing / highly reactive

questions.Question: Which communication environment feels most natural?
questions.Options / scale: Formal / moderately formal / balanced / informal / highly informal

questions.Question: Describe a work or study environment in which you performed especially well. What conditions helped?
Describe an environment that made it harder for you to perform. What specifically caused difficulty?
Which range best describes how much of your working time you would ideally and acceptably spend collaborating directly with others?
Which group role do you most often take naturally?
questions.Options / scale: Coordinator / idea generator / analyst / implementer / challenger / supporter / communicator / flexible

questions.Question: Describe a time another person’s delay or mistake affected your work. What did you do?
Describe a disagreement with a peer or project partner. How did you handle it?
When do you normally ask for help?
questions.Options / scale: Very early / after trying briefly / after several attempts / only when blocked / varies

questions.Question: Tell us about feedback that changed how you approached a task.
How comfortable are you challenging a decision made by someone more senior?
How do you prefer decisions to be made in a team?
questions.Options / scale: Leader decides / consult then decide / shared decision / varies by topic

questions.Question: Review the skills and tools extracted from your CV. Which are correct, missing or no longer current?
For each selected skill, what is your current level?
For each selected skill, when did you last use it?
What evidence best supports each important skill?
questions.Options / scale: Employment / project / course / portfolio / work sample / other

questions.Question: Review the tasks extracted from your CV. Which tasks have you actually performed?
For each task, how often and with how much independence did you perform it?
Choose up to three examples that best show what you can contribute to an employer.
For each example, what was the situation, your personal contribution and the result?
Which professional claims in your profile should not be shared with employers without asking you again?

structured_interview.Core question: What would make your next role a meaningful step rather than simply a job?
Which part of your preferred role do you understand least today?
Choose one capability you rated highly. Walk me through the most difficult example where you used it.
What part did you personally do, and what was done by others?
What would someone need to know before trusting you to do this independently?
Tell me about a task you initially did with support and later handled independently.
Describe a time the available information was incomplete. What did you do first?
Tell me about a recommendation you communicated to someone without your technical background.
Tell me about a team commitment that became at risk. How did you respond?
Describe a disagreement where you changed your own position.
Describe a disagreement where you did not change your position. How did you communicate it?
When have you waited too long to ask for help?
Tell me about an unclear assignment. What level of ambiguity was useful, and what became unproductive?
How do you react when priorities change after you have already invested significant effort?
Describe the best support you received from a manager, teacher or supervisor.
What made your most engaging project engaging after the initial excitement passed?
What would you be willing to compromise on in your first role, and what would you not compromise on?
Which part of your self-profile do you think might be wrong or incomplete?
Which claim should we treat cautiously until we collect more evidence?
What do you want SHEXON to explain to a company that your CV does not show well?
